core_obligations: If the element is good with respect to a maximal regular sequence, conclude directly from the good element lemma; this covers the case of dimension one (proof lines 25244-25247).

In higher dimension choose a further element h cutting the support down, argue on the quotients to show that both the chosen element and h act injectively, and combine this with the Cohen-Macaulayness of the double quotient (proof lines 25248-25265).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the good case and settle dimension one (proof lines 25243-25247).
Choose a second element and run the induction on the quotient (proof lines 25248-25266).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a Cohen-Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring, an element g whose vanishing cuts the support down by exactly one is a nonzerodivisor with Cohen-Macaulay quotient of depth one less (statement lines 25234-25241). The proof does not measure depths directly: it invokes the good element lemma when g is good with respect to a maximal regular sequence, and otherwise chooses a further element h cutting the support down, arguing on quotients that both g and h act injectively (proof lines 25243-25266). Finding the auxiliary element h so that the induction applies is the content. H2.
